Looking at this problem, I need to carefully track the collection through multiple transformations.

Let me write Python code to solve this step by step:

```python
# Define an Item class to track properties
class Item:
    def __init__(self, size, origin, name, material, smell, color):
        self.size = size
        self.origin = origin
        self.name = name
        self.material = material
        self.smell = smell
        self.color = color
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"{self.size} {self.origin} {self.name} ({self.material}, {self.smell}, {self.color})"

# Initialize the collection with 34 items
initial_items = [
    Item("extra-extra-small", "Mexican", "box", "steel", "chocolate", "brown"),
    Item("small", "Spanish", "scissors", "plastic", "citrus fruits", "crimson"),
    Item("medium", "Japanese", "bag", "glass", "popcorn", "gold"),
    Item("extra-extra-large", "Polish", "screwdriver", "ceramic", "wet dog", "gold"),
    Item("large", "German", "chair", "plastic", "vinegar", "gray"),
    Item("extra-large", "Turkish", "scissors", "ceramic", "burning wood", "green"),
    Item("small", "Polish", "house", "glass", "popcorn", "green"),
    Item("extra-small", "Portuguese", "stapler", "steel", "vanilla", "green"),
    Item("extra-large", "French", "bed", "ceramic", "leather", "green"),
    Item("medium", "Turkish", "camera", "steel", "garlic", "green"),
    Item("extra-extra-large", "Polish", "chair", "glass", "vanilla", "green"),
    Item("extra-extra-small", "Russian", "banana", "concrete", "vinegar", "indigo"),
    Item("medium", "Brazilian", "chair", "concrete", "citrus fruits", "indigo"),
    Item("medium", "Brazilian", "screwdriver", "glass", "gasoline", "ivory"),
    Item("extra-small", "Brazilian", "sunglasses", "concrete", "gasoline", "ivory"),
    Item("extra-extra-small", "Italian", "lamp", "plastic", "pine needles", "ivory"),
    Item("extra-small", "Mexican", "ruler", "concrete", "baking bread", "ivory"),
    Item("extra-large", "Chinese", "plate", "plastic", "citrus fruits", "orange"),
    Item("extra-small", "Brazilian", "trash can", "concrete", "baking bread", "orange"),
    Item("extra-small", "German", "plate", "glass", "coconut", "pink"),
    Item("medium", "Brazilian", "car", "glass", "gasoline", "purple"),
    Item("large", "French", "sunglasses", "steel", "chocolate", "purple"),
    Item("extra-extra-large", "Chinese", "guitar", "steel", "freshly cut grass", "red"),
    Item("extra-large", "German", "book", "plastic", "garlic", "silver"),
    Item("extra-extra-large", "Polish", "car", "concrete", "gasoline", "teal"),
    Item("large", "Chinese", "bag", "ceramic", "gasoline", "teal"),
    Item("extra-large", "Italian", "piano", "concrete", "citrus fruits", "turquoise"),
    Item("small", "Spanish", "bag", "ceramic", "baking bread", "turquoise"),
    Item("small", "Afghan", "ruler", "steel", "coffee", "turquoise"),
    Item("extra-extra-small", "Italian", "calculator", "glass", "burning wood", "violet"),
    Item("large", "Turkish", "earring", "ceramic", "garlic", "violet"),
    Item("medium", "Portuguese", "plier", "ceramic", "popcorn", "yellow"),
    Item("extra-large", "British", "watch", "plastic", "burning wood", "yellow"),
    Item("large", "Canadian", "umbrella", "ceramic", "freshly cut grass", "yellow"),
]

collection = initial_items[:]
initial_collection = initial_items[:]

# Step 1: Uncle throws away Canadian item, gives Portuguese and Italian versions
collection = [item for item in collection if item.origin != "Canadian"]
# Add Portuguese and Italian umbrellas (same as removed Canadian umbrella but different origin)
collection.append(Item("large", "Portuguese", "umbrella", "ceramic", "freshly cut grass", "yellow"))
collection.append(Item("large", "Italian", "umbrella", "ceramic", "freshly cut grass", "yellow"))

# Step 2: For each large item, replace with ceramic version with coconut smell
large_items = [item for item in collection if item.size == "large"]
for item in large_items:
    collection.remove(item)
    collection.append(Item(item.size, item.origin, item.name, "ceramic", "coconut", item.color))

# Step 3: Teacher throws away items where color starts with "b" or name has 6 characters
collection = [item for item in collection 
              if not (item.color.startswith("b") or len(item.name) == 6)]

# Step 4: Throw away all items where we have even count of that type
from collections import Counter
item_type_count = Counter(item.name for item in collection)
collection = [item for item in collection if item_type_count[item.name] % 2 == 1]

# Step 5: Fiancée adds copies of items with (smell, color) pairs not in initial collection
initial_smell_color = set((item.smell, item.color) for item in initial_collection)
current_smell_color = set((item.smell, item.color) for item in collection)
new_pairs = current_smell_color - initial_smell_color

items_to_add = []
for item in collection:
    if (item.smell, item.color) in new_pairs:
        items_to_add.append(Item(item.size, item.origin, item.name, item.material, item.smell, item.color))
collection.extend(items_to_add)

# Step 6: Lose one extra-small item
extra_small_items = [item for item in collection if item.size == "extra-small"]
if extra_small_items:
    collection.remove(extra_small_items[0])

# Final count: items with color not teal, size not extra-small, material not plastic, 
# smell not pine needles, origin not Japanese
count = 0
for item in collection:
    if (item.color != "teal" and 
        item.size != "extra-small" and 
        item.material != "plastic" and 
        item.smell != "pine needles" and 
        item.origin != "Japanese"):
        count += 1

print(f"ANSWER: {count}")
```
